Serum Ascites Albumin Gradient (SAAG)

SAAG

  • It is one of the investigations used to evaluate newly diagnosed or worsening ascites
  • It is used to distinguish the causes of ascites whether it is caused by portal hypertension or malignancy or other causes
  • Sample of the ascitic fluid is taken via paracentesis
  • And then the sample taken to laboratory to calculate albumin level and also sample of patient blood also taken for albumin level calculation
  • Then SAAG = serum albumin – ascites albumin
  • If SAAG > 1.1 g/dL
  • Means the albumin level in blood is much higher than the ascitic fluid
  • This means that the ascitic fluid is forming due to high pressure driving the fluid into the peritoneum (from the vessels into peritoneum)
  • This high pressure is caused by portal hypertension
  • Portal hypertension is caused by: liver cirrhosis, heart failure, Budd Chiari syndrome …
  • If SAAG < 1.1 g/dL
  • Means the albumin level in blood is little higher than the ascitic fluid
  • Here the problem is in the vessels, they are leaking the albumin and the fluid into the peritoneum
  • Causes: malignancy, infections, pancreatitis …

Total ascitic protein

  • Total protein of the ascitic fluid is used with the SAAG to identify the cause of ascites
  • Same ascites sample taken for SAAG is used to calculate total protein
  • If total ascitic protein < 2.5 g/dL
  • Total ascitic protein is low
  • Mostly due to portal hypertension, other causes include nephrotic syndrome and tuberculosis peritonitis
  • If total ascitic protein > 2.5 g/dL
  • Total ascitic protein is high
  • Causes include: heart failure, malignancy
Table from slide 9
SAAG
< 1.1 g/dL > 1.1 g/dL
Total protein < 2.5 g/dL Nephrotic syndrome Liver cirrhosis, Budd Chiari syndrome
> 2.5 g/dL Cancer, pancreatitis, infection Heart failure, veno occlusive disease
